'''Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys''' (IMFA) is a fully integrated Indian producer of [[ferrochrome]], headquartered in [[Bhubaneswar]], [[Odisha]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metal and Ferro Alloys: Well placed with integrated operations |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/earnings/indian-metal-and-ferro-alloys-well-placed-with-integrated-operations-11867111.html |website=Moneycontrol}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Mazumdar |first1=Rakhi |title=IMFA Group creates distinct business units as part of new organisation structure |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/metals-mining/imfa-group-creates-distinct-business-units-as-part-of-new-organisation-structure/articleshow/19364152.cms |website=Economic Times |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=3 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys shares climb 120% in 1 year: CFO Prem Khandelwal explains why - Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys shares climb 120% in 1 year: CFO Prem Khandelwal explains why BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/indian-metals-ferro-alloys-shares-climb-120-in-1-year-cfo-prem-khandelwal-explains-why-437480-2024-07-17 |website=BusinessToday.in |publisher=[[Business Today (India)]] |language=en |date=17 July 2024}}</ref>

Ferrochrome is primarily used in the production of stainless steel.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Law |first1=Abhishek |title=Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys expects to maintain margins at 25 per cent in H1FY23 |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/imfa-expects-to-maintain-margins-at-25-per-cent-in-h1fy23/article65477053.ece |website=ThehinduBusinessLine |publisher=[[Business Line]] |language=en |date=31 May 2022}}</ref> IMFA exports its Ferrochrome to [[Korea|South Korea]], [[China]], [[Japan]] and [[Taiwan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Share Price Today, 878.45, Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Stock Price 878.45 on 13th Jan 2025, Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Stock Price Live NSE/BSE {{!}} Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/indian-metals-ferro-alloys-ltd-share-price-5807.html |website=business-standard.com |publisher=[[Business Standard]]}}</ref>

Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Limited is a listed company in the [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]] and [[Bombay Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys Ltd, IMFA:NSI profile - FT.com |url=https://markets.ft.com/data/equities/tearsheet/profile?s=IMFA:NSI |website=markets.ft.com |publisher=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref>

==History==
Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys (IMFA) was established in 1961 by Bansidhar Panda and Ila Panda. Bansidhar Panda completed advanced degrees from [[Michigan Technological University]] and [[Harvard University]], before returning to Odisha to establish a [[ferroalloy]] plant at [[Therubali]]. His wife, Ila Panda, an alumna of [[Visva-Bharati University]], supported the venture as was a patron of art and literature.<ref>{{cite web |title=Industrialist and founder of IMFA Bansidhar Panda passes away at 87 |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2018/May/22/industrialist-and-founder-of-imfa-bansidhar-panda-passes-away-at-87-1818037.html#:~:text=BHUBANESWAR:%20Noted%20industrialist%20and%20founder%20of%20Indian,growth%20of%20the%20State%20by%20using%20its |website=The New Indian Express |language=en |date=22 May 2018}}</ref>

In 1967, IMFA commenced the manufacture of [[ferrosilicon]] in Odisha. The company later became the first firm in the Indian subcontinent to manufacture silicon metal using proprietary technology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Department Of Energy Conservation |url=https://eicelectricityodisha.nic.in/ECONS/detail_pages/imfatherubali.aspx |website=eicelectricityodisha.nic.in}}</ref>

==Operation==
As of 2 March 2026, IMFA has an installed furnace capacity of 289 MVA capable of producing 434,000 tonnes per annum (tpa), making it the largest value-added ferrochrome producer of the country.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 19, 2026 |title=IMFA bets on ferro chrome expansion, renewables for next growth phase |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/imfa-bets-on-ferro-chrome-expansion-renewables-for-next-growth-phase-126051901662_1.html |website=Business Standard}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IMFA acquires Tata Steel ferro chrome plant |url=https://www.constructionweekonline.in/business/imfa-acquires-tata-steel-ferro-chrome-plant |website=Constructionweekonline}}</ref>

In February 2026, the company completed the strategic acquisition of [[Tata Steel|Tata Steel Limited]]’s (TSL) ferrochrome plant in [[Kalinganagar]], Odisha. The transaction is valued at {{Currency|707|INR}} crore, including a base consideration of {{Currency|610|INR|linked=no}} crore, along with GST and net working capital, and was funded entirely through internal accruals. The land area occupied by the plant is around 115 acres and includes four furnaces with an annual production capacity of 100,000 tonnes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Feb 27, 2026 |title=IMFA completes ferro chrome plant acquisition from Tata Steel at Rs 707 crore transaction |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/steel/imfa-completes-ferro-chrome-plant-acquisition-from-tata-steel-at-rs-707-crore-transaction/articleshow/128857555.cms?from=mdr&utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Economic Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IMFA completes acquisition of Tata Steel’s ferro chrome plant |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2026/Feb/28/imfa-completes-acquisition-of-tata-steels-ferro-chrome-plant |website=The New Indian Express |language=en |date=28 February 2026}}</ref>

IMFA operates captive chrome ore mines at [[Sukinda]] and Mahagiri, along with manufacturing complexes at [[Therubali]], [[Choudwar]] and [[Kalinganagar]]. It also has captive power generation comprising 200 MW from coal-based sources and 4.55 MW from solar.<ref>{{cite web |title=IMFA reports robust Q3 FY26 results |url=https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/IMFA_05022026142341_Press_release_IMFA_Q3FY26_results.pdf |website=NSEIndia}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Share Price Today, 878.45, Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Stock Price 878.45 on 13th Jan 2025, Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd Stock Price Live NSE/BSE {{!}} Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/indian-metals-ferro-alloys-ltd-share-price-5807.html |website=www.business-standard.com |publisher=[[Business Standard]]}}</ref>

As part of its diversification strategy, a 120 KLD grain-based ethanol plant is being set up at Therubali, Odisha.{{Update inline|date=April 2026}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Metals MD says expansion will be funded via internal accruals - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/indian-metals-and-ferro-alloys-md-subhrakant-panda-dividend-payout-expansion-diversification-plans-19391073.htm |website=CNBCTV18.com |publisher=[[CNBC TV18]] |language=en |date=2 April 2024}}</ref>

In December 2024, IMFA partnered with [[JSW Energy|JSW Green Energy One Ltd]] and JSW Green Energy Seven Ltd to source renewable energy for its smelting operations, consisting of 50 MW AC solar and 100 MW wind power. In May 2026, IMFA signed a 29-year captive PPA for 65 MW of hybrid renewable power usage in its ferrochrome production facilities. With the addition of the new project, the company’s total contracted renewable energy portfolio has increased to 135 MW.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 26, 2026 |title=Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys acquires 26% stake in EG Urja Strot for ₹110 cr |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/imfa-acquires-26-stake-in-eg-urja-strot-for-110-crore-to-bolster-renewable-energy-strategy/131327559?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=ET Energy World}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IMFA partners with JSW Green Energy for renewable power in smelting operations - ET EnergyWorld |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/imfa-partners-with-jsw-green-energy-for-renewable-power-in-smelting-operations/116456705 |website=ETEnergyworld.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2026 |title=IMFA Acquires 26% Stake In EG Urja Strot, Secures 65 MW Hybrid Renewable Power |url=https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/imfa-acquires-26-stake-in-eg-urja-strot-secures-65-mw-hybrid-renewable-power-11878340?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Saura Energy}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
===Sarala Puraskar===
Sarala Puraskar is presented annually in recognition of outstanding contributions to the Odia language and literature. This award has been conferred since 1980 under the aegis of the Indian Metals Public Charitable Trust (IMPaCT), and managed by IMFA.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sahoo |first1=Akshaya Kumar |title=Eminent Poet And Writer Devdas Chhotray To Receive 46th Sarala Puraskar |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/eminent-poet-and-writer-devdas-chhotray-to-receive-46th-sarala-puraskar-1903904 |website=www.deccanchronicle.com |language=en |date=15 September 2025}}</ref>

===Ekalabya Puraskar===
Ekalabya Puraskar, instituted in 1993 by IMPaCT, and managed by IMFA. This award aims to encourage young sportspersons from Odisha. It is regarded as one of the most prestigious recognitions in the field of sports in the state.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ekalabya Puraskar for budding badminton star Swetaparna Panda |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2025/Oct/12/ekalabya-puraskar-for-budding-badminton-star-swetaparna-panda |website=The New Indian Express |publisher=[[The New Indian Express]] |language=en |date=12 October 2025}}</ref>
